lines.text: Four and a half billion years ago, the Earth was young, and it was on fire. Volcanoes poured out molten rock, and the sky filled with steam.
As the planet cooled, the steam fell as rain. It rained for an unimaginably long time, and the rain filled the first oceans.
For billions of years, the land stayed bare. No trees, no grass. Only rock, wind and waves. Life had begun, but only in the sea, far too small to see.
Ice ages came and went. Great sheets of ice crept across the land, and slowly melted away again.
When the last ice age ended, about twelve thousand years ago, wild grasses spread across warm hills. Among them grew a plant that would change everything. Wild wheat.
And that is where our story begins.
